Hi Dev —

Thanks for running through the private deployment options with us last week. Our security team is preparing the firewall and egress controls for a potential VPC-hosted private endpoint. Before we start change windows on our side we need a consolidated list of: 1) IP addresses and/or domain names we must allow out from our VPC, 2) recommended firewall rules for inbound control to the private endpoint, and 3) guidance on how egress from the model runtime is handled (do tokens or inference payloads leave our VPC?).

We'd like to provide this to our network ops tomorrow. Can you send a short playbook and any artifacts (sample ip ranges, expected ports, TLS/FQDNs) we can hand to our firewall team? Also flag anything that requires a maintenance window or NAT changes.

Nadia —

Thanks for the clear list. I'm attaching our internal private deployment checklist (redwood_private_requirements_v1.pdf) and looping in Laura (solutions) and Marissa (sales/legal) to confirm contract/operational items. High-level notes up front:

- Redwood's private endpoints are run inside your VPC (customer-managed). Under typical setups, outbound egress is controlled by customer NAT or firewall. We publish a small set of destination domains and optional static IP ranges for allowlisting if you need tight egress controls.
- Inbound access to the private endpoint should be limited to your application subnets or a single jump host; we recommend security-group style allowlisting by source IP/subnet.
- We do not keep inference payloads in our hosted control plane for private deployments unless you opt into telemetry; we can provide a data handling statement for the agreement.

Next steps: Laura — can you paste the exact domains/IPs and port requirements here so Nadia's team can get started? Marissa — please call out if we need explicit contract language or a data processing addendum.

I'll schedule a 30-minute ops alignment if that helps (proposed Tue 10am PT).

Best,

Cc: Nadia Khan <nadia.khan@finserve.co>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Private deployment egress & firewall questions

Dev / Nadia —

Thanks — quick technical summary for ops. Paste this to your firewall team:

1) Outbound (egress) destinations you may need to allow
- Required domains (DNS FQDNs):
  - runtime-api.redwood-inference.com (HTTPS 443) — control plane calls for model metadata and model variant negotiation.
  - telemetry.redwood-inference.com (HTTPS 443) — optional; only used if telemetry is enabled.
- Optional static IP ranges (for environments that cannot do DNS allowlisting):
  - 52.26.101.120/32
  - 34.210.45.88/31
  - 54.184.33.10/32
  Note: We recommend DNS allowlisting when possible; IPs are subject to change and will be versioned in the URL below.
- Ports: 443 outbound (HTTPS). No other tcp/udp ports are required for normal inference traffic.

2) Inbound (to customer-hosted private endpoint)
- The private endpoint exposes an HTTPS endpoint on port 443 inside your VPC (private IP). Limit inbound to:
  - your app subnet CIDRs or specific jump host IPs.
  - If you have a WAF, allow only POST /v1/generate and block other uncommon verbs.
- Mutual TLS: supported on request. If you require mTLS, we will provide cert fingerprints and an onboarding window.

3) Egress from model runtime
- Model inference executes in compute within your VPC/subnet. By default, the runtime can make outbound HTTPS calls to the control plane for management (model version checks). No user prompt content is sent to third parties by Redwood.
- If you enable external tool-calls (webhooks or integrations) those can cause outbound requests to external hosts; treat them as separate and restrict via egress rules.

4) Logging, auditing, and retention
- Access logs and audit events can be configured to stream to your S3/logging endpoint. We support pushing audit logs to a customer-owned bucket or allowing your SIEM to pull from our telemetry endpoint (if enabled).

Operational notes:
- If you need fully air-gapped operation, we offer an on-prem package; that requires a slightly different install and contract.
- We publish an allowlist.json at the internal deploy doc (link below) with timestamped IP lists. Tell your ops team to pull that URL during maintenance windows.

Reference link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-example-private-deploy

If this looks good I'll join the ops call and walk through the NAT/firewall change window.

Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

--
Note: the IPs above are maintained and rotated quarterly. If you cannot rely on DNS allowlisting, we'll coordinate a scheduled maintenance window to update IPs on your firewall.

Looping in a quick commercial note so Nadia has visibility.

- Data handling / contract: We need to ensure the DPA covers that telemetry is optional and that FinServe owns audit logs they export to their S3. I'll add a clause to the SOW clarifying that runtime inference data stays in-customer VPC and that the control plane interactions are limited to the domains below.
- SLA & egress outages: If FinServe chooses DNS allowlisting and an IP rotation causes a brief interruption, standard Dedicated SLA remedies apply but we will also schedule a proactive notification window. For Private (VPC) deployments we can add a 24-hour rotation notice to the SOW if you need it.
